Without the change, the base Config::parse would reject this, so the test would fail.

findings.summary: Admission now compiles candidate-supplied code on the host
findings.evidence: Admission runs `cargo run` on the candidate's crates/athena-data/ with no sandbox. A candidate that adds a build.rs or changes the crate's code gets that code executed by the Athena process during admission. The accepted reading allowed building the candidate's crate, and Athena's checks already build candidate trees, so this is a risk to note rather than a defect.

findings.summary: The checker shares CARGO_TARGET_DIR with the running build and drops RUSTFLAGS
findings.evidence: When CARGO_TARGET_DIR is set, it is inherited and RUSTFLAGS is removed. That can make cargo rebuild athena-data and its dependencies in the shared target directory, and it can contend for the build lock with concurrent jobs. A dedicated subdirectory would avoid both.

findings.summary: Landing still parses with the running Config
findings.evidence: CHANGELOG.md notes this, as the reading asked, but there is no follow-up beyond that note. A landed schema change takes effect only after Athena is rebuilt.

summary: The change fixes the root cause. When a candidate changes crates/athena-data/, admission now checks a changed athena.toml or defaults.toml against the candidate's own schema instead of the schema compiled into the running Athena. It does this by writing the candidate's athena-data crate, root Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock to a temporary directory, building a small checker against them offline, and running it on the file. If the checker cannot be built or run, admission reports a 'configuration' violation with the real error. When the schema is not touched, admission parses with the running schema as before. Three new tests cover three cases: a section added together with its schema field is admitted, an unknown section is still refused under both paths, and a broken candidate schema is a violation. The first and third would fail without the change. The first also reproduces the exact `unknown field `parallel`` refusal that the jobs q0xy and qcrz met. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core admission` (9 passed) and fmt, clippy and the full `cargo test --locked` (all passed) in this snapshot. CHANGELOG.md names the root cause and notes that landing has the same flaw. Only admission.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed, and both are on the deliverables list. I have minor notes only: admission now compiles candidate-supplied code (for example an added build.rs) on the host, and it shares CARGO_TARGET_DIR with the running build.
